pages.summary: Patterns of text, built from parts: what the text functions search for, as readable pieces instead of a regular expression.
body: A pattern is text to match, or one of the character patterns: digits, letters, letters and digits, white space, any characters, or one of a list of characters. With a count `n`, exactly that many; with `min` and `max`, between them; otherwise as many as there are (wildcards as few as will do). Patterns join with `+` (one after the other) and give alternatives with `|`. `contains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `matches`, `count`, `strfind`, `replace`, `erase`, `split`, `extract`, `extractBefore`, `extractAfter`, `extractBetween`, `insertBefore` and `insertAfter` take them.
syntax: Text as a pattern; `p1 + p2` matches one after the other, `p1 | p2` either.
One of a list of characters.

examples.title: Numbers, words and codes taken out of text
examples.code:
s = "Order 12 shipped to room B-204 on 5 Nov";
extract(s, digitsPattern)
extract(s, lettersPattern(4, Inf))
extract(s, characterListPattern("A", "Z") + "-" + digitsPattern(3))
contains(["a1", "bb", "c22"], digitsPattern)
examples.output:
ans =

  3×1 string array

    "12"
    "204"
    "5"

ans =

  3×1 string array

    "Order"
    "shipped"
    "room"

ans =

    "B-204"

ans =

  1×3 logical array

   1   0   1

examples.title: Wildcards, and alternatives
examples.code: extract("one and two", "" + wildcardPattern + "") replace("cat, dog, cow", "cat" | "cow", "animal") extract("key=value; name=pylab", lettersPattern + "=" + lettersPattern) extract("f(x), g(y, z)", "(" + wildcardPattern('Except', "()") + ")")
examples.output: ans = 2×1 string array "one" "two" ans = "animal, dog, animal" ans = 2×1 string array "key=value" "name=pylab" ans = 2×1 string array "(x)" "(y, z)"

pages.summary: Patterns repeated: once or not at all, as many times as possible, or as few as will do.
body: `optionalPattern(p)` matches p or nothing; `asManyOfPattern(p, min, max)` repeats p as many times as it can (between min and max when given); `asFewOfPattern(p, min, max)` as few times as lets the rest match.

examples.title: Signs, repeats, and the shortest match
examples.code:
num = optionalPattern("-") + digitsPattern;
extract("5, -12 and 7", num)
extract("aaab", asManyOfPattern("a", 1, 2))
extract("[1][2]", "[" + asFewOfPattern(wildcardPattern(1), 1, 5) + "]")
examples.output:
ans =

  3×1 string array

    "5"
    "-12"
    "7"

ans =

  2×1 string array

    "aa"
    "a"

ans =

  2×1 string array

    "[1]"
    "[2]"

pages.summary: Boundaries: places in text that patterns match without taking any characters.
body: Where letters, digits, letters and digits, or white space start, end, or either (`type` `'start'`, `'end'` or `'either'`, the default); the start or end of a line or of the whole text; and where a pattern comes next (`lookAheadBoundary`) or just before (`lookBehindBoundary`, of a fixed length). They anchor a pattern without becoming part of the match.
syntax: The start or end of a line.
The start or end of the text.

examples.title: Whole words, line starts, and what comes before a unit
examples.code:
s = "cat category scat";
count(s, "cat")
count(s, letterBoundary + "cat" + letterBoundary)
lines = "a: 1" + newline + "b: 2";
extract(lines, lineBoundary('start') + lettersPattern)
extract("5 kg, 12 m, 7 kg", digitsPattern + lookAheadBoundary(" kg"))
extract("$12 and €30", lookBehindBoundary("€") + digitsPattern)
examples.output:
ans =

     3

ans =

     1

ans =

  2×1 string array

    "a"
    "b"

ans =

  2×1 string array

    "5"
    "7"

ans =

    "30"

pages.summary: Patterns from a regular expression, patterns matched whatever the case, and patterns with a name.
body: `regexpPattern(expr)` makes a pattern of a regular expression, to combine with others. `caseInsensitivePattern(p)` matches p in any case (and `caseSensitivePattern` only in its own). `namedPattern(p, name)` gives a pattern a name it is shown by.

examples.title: A date by regular expression, and words in any case
examples.code:
date = regexpPattern('\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}');
extract("from 2026-11-05 to 2026-12-24", date)
count("Error, ERROR, error", caseInsensitivePattern("error"))
p = namedPattern(digitsPattern, "number")
examples.output:
ans =

  2×1 string array

    "2026-11-05"
    "2026-12-24"

ans =

     3

p = 

  pattern

  Matching:

    number

pages.summary: The parts of text that match a pattern, or characters by position.
body: For one text, a column of the matches; for several texts, an array when each has one match, else a cell array. A number takes the character at that position.

examples.title: Matches and positions
examples.output:
ans =

  3×1 string array

    "1"
    "22"
    "333"

ans =

  1×2 string array

    "1"    "22"

ans =

    "ho"
